claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar colony microstructure.
The starting alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
Dislocation accumulation at internal boundaries causes the starting alloy's limited ductility and brittleness.
A rapid post-solidification aging treatment can trigger fine coherent precipitate formation along the lamellar interfaces.
The treatment will produce nanoscale coherent precipitates selectively at lamellar boundaries.
The boundary precipitates will act as dislocation absorbers.
The boundary precipitates will enhance dislocation transmission across internal boundaries.
Enhanced absorption and transmission will reduce dislocation buildup at internal boundaries.
Reduced dislocation buildup will lower local stress concentrations.
Lower local stress concentrations will delay microcrack nucleation.
The treated alloy will have significantly greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain or moderately enhance tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy fails catastrophically at room temperature through dislocation pile-ups and microcracking along lamellar interfaces.
Excessive precipitate coarsening or a nonuniform precipitate distribution could impair ductility or adversely affect strength.
The proposed treatment is applicable to room-temperature tensile testing under ambient conditions and conventional loading rates.
Analogous material systems support the expected improvements in ductility and strength.
